title: No Nut November vs Your Prostate: Science
description:
No Nut November vs your prostate: what does the science actually say? Cyto breaks it down from the 6ix.

A 2025 meta-analysis pooled 29 studies (315,193 men). Higher ejaculation frequency was linked to lower prostate cancer risk (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.77-0.90). Masturbation frequency alone was not significantly linked (OR 1.12, 95% CI 0.82-1.54), and intercourse frequency, number of partners and age at first intercourse showed no significant link. A 2025 systematic review (10 studies) found lower risk with more frequent intercourse (5-12+ times a month) but a possible risk increase with very frequent masturbation (2-7+ times a week) and with more lifetime partners.

The limits: these are observational studies of long-term habits, not a one-month challenge. Linked, not proven. Nothing here says a month of the challenge is good or bad for you.

Sources (via PubMed):
Raeisvandi et al., BMC Cancer 2025 - https://doi.org/10.1186/s12885-025-15410-3
Firsty et al., Asian Pac J Cancer Prev 2025 - https://doi.org/10.31557/APJCP.2025.26.9.3193

Not medical advice. Urinary symptoms that worry you (trouble peeing, blood in your urine)? See a doctor. Men over 50, or with a family history, can ask their doctor about prostate screening.

Sources (via PubMed):
Raeisvandi A et al., Updated dose-response meta-analysis of sexual activity and prostate cancer risk, BMC Cancer 2025, PMID 41345847, https://doi.org/10.1186/s12885-025-15410-3 | Firsty NN et al., Preceding sexual behavior in younger years and prostate cancer occurrence, Asian Pac J Cancer Prev 2025, PMID 40952273, https://doi.org/10.31557/APJCP.2025.26.9.3193
